extracted.intended_audience: literate readers of The Spectator; general public interested in manners, morals, and periodical essays (early-18th-century)
extracted.subtask_description: Producing short, conversational moral and social essays (Spectator-style) that comment on manners, education, gossip, and public life, mixing humor, anecdote, and moral reflection. Also includes proposals for periodical news/whisper columns and guidance on rhetorical devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newsworthiness: 'Whispers' (secret + scandal)
rubrics_metrics.description: By Whispers I mean those Pieces of News which are communicated as Secrets, and which bring a double Pleasure to the Hearer; first, as they are private History, and in the next place as they have always in them a Dash of Scandal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materials to deal in: sickness of Persons in high Posts; Twilight Visits paid and received by Ministers of State; Clandestine Courtships and Marriages; Secret Amours; Losses at Play; Applications for Places, with their respective Successes or Repulses. Whispers should feel private and titillating; they gain traction because people desire to be 'in the Secret.' (Example characters: Peter Hush — a coffee-house whisperer; Lady Blast — spreads damaging whispers about women.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness and distribution of gossip/news
rubrics_metrics.description: A good whisper/news-item is launched quickly and spread through social hubs (coffee-houses) to reach audiences at different times and places.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use informants who frequent public venues; publish/semi-publish early in the day at key locations (example chronology given: by eight at Garraway's, by twelve at Will's, before two at the Smyrna). Having representative, well-placed sources (e.g., 'a whispering Hole in most of the great Coffee-houses') is integral to circulation and perceived authority of the gossip.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Similes — avoid gross and ignorant comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: Admonishes all Persons ... how they discover their Ignorance in the Use of Similes. Gross Abuses in this Kind expose the speaker's ignorance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make literal or ridiculous comparisons that betray ignorance of the compared subject (example of poor usage: 'One would think, like the Elephant, you had no Knees' — showing the speaker's error by literal misapplication). Preachers, barristers, and public speakers should avoid careless or ill-informed similes; offenders may be publicly noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: True Modesty vs False Modesty (moral criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: True Modesty is ashamed to do any thing that is repugnant to the Rules of right Reason: False Modesty is ashamed to do any thing that is opposite to the Humour of the Company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify false modesty by behavior that sacrifices reason or virtue to avoid singularity or to comply with fashion (examples: lending beyond means, giving recommendations for strangers, accepting improper favors). False modesty can lead to indiscreet or criminal actions; prefer sincere, visible virtue — be 'sincerely Virtuous, and at the same time let the World see we are so.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Education as cultivation — nurture intellectual talents like plants
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a sort of vegetable Principle in the Mind of every Man when he comes into the World... the Leaves (Words) → Flowers (fancy) → Fruit (philosophy, mathematics, close Reasoning). Many Virtues are choked by Weeds or starved by wrong Soil; proper Manuring, Pruning, and Artful Management are necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good education requires discovering and properly tending 'seeds' of talent: remove weeds, choose appropriate soil, prune and manure (i.e., give correct guidance and discipline). Beware spending life on merely collecting leaves/flowers (superficial accomplishments) rather than cultivating fruit (substantial learning and reasoning).

rubrics_metrics.name: Value of reviewing the unlearned (satirical critical target)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal: publish monthly 'An Account of the Works of the Unlearned' to review and expose the productions of those who make an 'eminent Figure in the Illiterate World.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Target party-authors, editors, commentators often 'Men of no learning, or, what is as bad, of no Knowledge.' Reviewing such works is a legitimate project: it can lampoon pretension and serve public taste by distinguishing genuine learning from vanity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essayist's observational stance: keep mind open to gratification
rubrics_metrics.description: It is of great Use, if they could learn with me to keep their Minds open to Gratification, and ready to receive it from any thing it meets with.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt speculative curiosity: value things as objects of speculation rather than solely for worldly advantage. Actively observe and receive small pleasures from everyday scenes (markets, coffee-houses, faces), which increases personal happiness and supplies material for essays. Polite social gestures (e.g., saluting agreeable persons) and attentiveness are recommended as sources of amusement and moral reflection.
